articles.title: Bengaluru lawyer drags sister out of house, beats her to death with cricket bat
articles.summary: Bengaluru lawyer Jayaram, 42, allegedly killed sister Meenakshi, 39, with a cricket bat in Bellandur amid a house dispute; police hunt underway.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A bitter dispute over a house allegedly ended in murder when a 42-year-old lawyer dragged his younger sister out of their house and battered her to death with a cricket bat in Bellandur Wednesday morning. The accused allegedly fled after she collapsed unconscious on the road.The deceased, Meenakshi, 39, had been living in her parental home for the past few years with her mother and two daughters in Junnasandra. Her elder brother, Jayaram, 42, a lawyer, had allegedly been repeatedly harassing her and pressuring her to vacate the sheet-roofed house and move elsewhere.According to Meenakshi’s mother, Jayaram lived on the first floor of their building, while she and Meenakshi stayed in an adjacent building. He had repeatedly insisted that Meenakshi vacate the house and live separately. However, both Meenakshi and her mother opposed his demand and continued staying together.On Wednesday morning, the siblings reportedly had another argument over the same issue. Jayaram allegedly dragged Meenakshi out of the house and attacked her with a cricket bat around 11.30am, leaving her critically injured. Her two daughters, who tried to intervene and stop him from assaulting their mother, were also allegedly attacked.A senior police officer said Jayaram escaped from the scene after Meenakshi fell unconscious on the road.Bellandur police rushed to the spot after receiving information and shifted the body to the mortuary for a post-mortem examination.A murder case has been registered at Bellandur police station, and efforts are on to nab Jayaram. “We will know the exact reason for the murder only after catching him,” a senior police officer said.Meenakshi was working as a tailor at a shop and had been separated from her husband a few years ago.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: 'Play with the ball that you've got': Tom Latham pushes back on Shubman Gill's concerns over ball quality
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes the condition of a cricket ball is influenced by the nature of the pitch, whether it is a Dukes or Kookaburra, but
articles.body: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes the condition of a cricket ball is influenced by the nature of the pitch, whether it is a Dukes or Kookaburra, but said players must learn to adapt rather than look for excuses.Latham's comments came after India captain Shubman Gill raised concerns over the quality of cricket balls following the drawn first Test in Wellington. Gill had said that both Dukes and Kookaburra balls tend to become soft after the first 25-30 overs, affecting their effectiveness.Speaking ahead of the second Test against India, Latham said the surface can play a role in how quickly the ball wears out and teams need to find ways to keep it in good condition."I think sometimes the wicket can dictate what the ball does, whether it's a little bit flatter or a little bit more abrasive, then the ball can deteriorate a little bit quicker, whether that be a Dukes ball, whether that be a Kookaburra ball," Latham said on the eve of the second Test against India."So I think from our point of view, we're always trying to adapt and find what's the best way to look after the ball to keep it in good condition as much as we can."Latham expects the ball to retain its condition for longer at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, given the nature of the surface and the limited cricket played at the venue recently."I think we'll probably see here (Christchurch) throughout the game that it will probably stay newer for longer because of the green surfaces."And there hasn't been a lot of cricket played out here at Hagley, so there's not a lot of used wickets that can deteriorate the ball quicker," he said.The New Zealand skipper also pointed out that the condition of cricket balls can vary between series and seasons, but said players have to work with what they are given."So, I guess it's a series-by-series thing. Sometimes it's a year-by-year thing. Sometimes the balls can be really good. Sometimes maybe not so good, where they deteriorate a little bit more."But we know as cricketers, you've got to be able to play with the ball that you've got. And whether it's in good condition, whether it's not so good, you've got to find a way," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ILT20: Dubai Capitals beat Desert Vipers by 45 runs, register first win of season 5
articles.summary: Dubai Capitals defeated Desert Vipers by 45 runs at the Dubai International Stadium on Wednesday to register their first win of ILT20 season 5.
articles.body: Dubai Capitals defeated Desert Vipers by 45 runs at the Dubai International Stadium on Wednesday to register their first win of ILT20 season 5.Sam Billings' 43 off 31 balls and Rovman Powell's rapid 28 off 12 powered the Capitals to 164/7, before the bowlers took over. Noor Ahmad's four for 20 and Mustafizur Rahman's two for 12 led the way, with Dushmantha Chameera (2/27) and Hassan Khan (2/16) also taking two wickets each as the Vipers were bowled out for 119 in 17.5 overs. Andries Gous's 27 off 30 was the Vipers' top score.Put in to bat first, Dubai Capitals suffered an early blow when Masood Gurbaz (2 off 2) was run out after a mix-up with Faf du Plessis (24 off 30) to leave them at 8/1. Max Holden (22 off 17) joined du Plessis and steered the innings through the powerplay, with a stand of 37 runs in 34 balls.The partnership didn't last as Vipers skipper Shadab Khan had Max Holden caught in the seventh. Soon after, du Plessis, was stumped off Nangeyalia Khan in search of his first boundary of the innings.The Capitals were 61/3 in 9.4 overs when Sam Billings (43 off 31) and Marcus Stoinis (27 off 24) came together for a key stand of 59 runs in 40 balls. With boundaries hard to come by, Billings broke the shackles in the 16th to smash Shadab for a six and two fours.Just as the Capitals looked set for a big finish, Khuzaima Tanveer removed Stoinis to leave the score at 120/4 in 16.2 overs. He then scalped Billings and Karim Janat (6 off 4) in the 19th over to emerge as the pick of the Vipers attack and take over the White Belt (awarded to the best bowler) with eight wickets in three innings.Rovman Powell (28 off 12) provided the finishing touch with a rapid-fire knock, smashing two fours and two sixes including 16 in the final over to catapult the Capitals to 164/7 in 20 overs.In response, the Vipers lost Babar Azam (1 off 2) in the second over off Dushmantha Chameera's bowling to leave them at 2/1. Fakhar Zaman (12 off 11) and Andries Gous added 35 before Fakhar was caught off Mustafizur Rahman in the fifth over, making it 37/2.Noor Ahmad then took charge, removing Joe Clarke (3 off 5) in the seventh and Gous (27 off 30) in the ninth over to leave the Vipers on 48/4.Shimron Hetmyer (19 off 13) and Shadab (16 off 11) tried to rebuild with a 31-run stand, but Chameera ended it by having the Vipers skipper caught in the 12th over. Noor had Hetmyer stumped in the 13th, leaving the Vipers at 83/6.Tom Curran (18 off 8) briefly raised hopes with two fours and a six, but he was caught off Noor for his fourth wicket in the 15th over to make it 102/7.Hassan Khan then struck twice in the 17th with the wickets of Khuzaima Tanveer (9 off 7) and Nangeyalia Khan (6 off 12). Mustafizur returned to dismiss Mujeeb Ur Rahman (2 off 4) as the Vipers were bowled out for 119 in 17.5 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'You have to make the new ball count': India coach challenges pacers to do more with the new Kookaburra ahead of must-win Test
articles.summary: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged the fast bowlers to make the most of the new Kookaburra ball, saying they need to be willing to take risks, as
articles.body: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged the fast bowlers to make the most of the new Kookaburra ball, saying they need to be willing to take risks, as India prepare for the must-win Test in Christchurch to keep their WTC final hopes alive."You have to make the new ball count. You need to be brave sometimes," Morkel said on the eve of the second and final Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.Morkel also backed Anshul Kamboj, who faced questions over his pace during the opening Test in Wellington. Kamboj bowled 45 overs across the two innings, but his speed dropped below 130 kmph during his second and third spells as India struggled to find breakthroughs on a surface that lost pace early.Morkel said it was unfair to single out the Haryana pacer, who had helped India maintain control through his bowling."Anshul did a great job. It is quite hard to judge from the outside...sitting in the dressing room, after the second day, if the wicketkeeper is standing up to a bowler who is two metres tall, that is worrying," Morkel said."Anshul gave us control. Let's support the guy as he bowls hard overs for the team.""The wicket lost a lot of pace early and hence the drop in pace of the bowlers. Wickets can get flat but you don't want them to lose pace ," he explained.With questions over India's pace-bowling resources and workload, Morkel said all the fast bowlers were fit and available, with the team set to make a selection call on the eve of the Test."All bowlers are fit and available and we will take a call tomorrow," he said.Morkel also addressed Mohammed Siraj's omission from the first Test, saying the senior pacer needed to assess his game and identify areas for improvement."Siraj is bowling well. Sometimes decisions are tough ones. My conversation with him was, 'Listen, let's step back a little and see where we can improve.' Selection, we can't control," Morkel said.The bowling coach said India needed to look beyond individual sessions and remain focused on the bigger objective of qualifying for the World Test Championship final."All these guys want to play the WTC final. After every bad session, we can't just get caught up. We have to break it down session by session and play our best brand of cricket," he said.Morkel also said Gurnoor Brar was pushing for a place in the team but needed to remain ready for when an opportunity came his way."Gurnoor is knocking on the door, doing all the right things. He has pace, bounce and will be ideal for these conditions. He just needs to be ready as and when he gets the opportunity. My job is to keep him 100 per cent ready," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd Test: Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep or Gurnoor Brar? Team India face selection dilemma ahead of Christchurch Test
articles.summary: At around 6.33am India time on Tuesday, three days before the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, came a terse 13-word
articles.body: At around 6.33am India time on Tuesday, three days before the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, came a terse 13-word WhatsApp alert from the BCCI media team: “Nov 25, 2026 - Christchurch. India. No practice and no press conference. Thank you.”It was hardly unexpected. With just a three-day turnaround between the two Tests, including a travel day, India were never going to exert themselves immediately after sending down a combined 241 overs across New Zealand’s two innings at the Basin Reserve. The training blocks and practice games are behind them. India will have just one training session, on Thursday, before the second Test, and it is now all about recovery, selection and execution.India went into the Basin Test with four seamers, Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Prasidh Krishna and Anshul Kamboj, and every one of them put in a significant shift, often having to operate into Wellington’s unforgiving wind. Bumrah sent down 49 overs, Kamboj and Prasidh 45 each and Akash 43.After Monday’s dispiriting draw in a Test they had controlled for long periods, skipper Shubman Gill hinted that India may not tinker too much with their XI or, more pertinently, the combination.There is certainly little in Hagley’s history to encourage them to move away from a paceheavy attack. In the 15 men’s Tests played at the venue, 444 of the 484 wickets have gone to pacers. That’s a massive 91.7%.So four quicks again? Certainly. But will they be the same four?India’s batters appear to be in decent touch, with several of them also having had useful time in the middle here during the India ‘A’ game. It is the bowling attack where the more intriguing calls lie.Could the team management be tempted to hand the nippy Gurnoor Brar a Test debut in place of Anshul Kamboj? Kamboj had a decent outing with bat and ball at the Basin, but when the ball became older and New Zealand’s batters dug in, he appeared a little short of the variations required to keep prising out wickets.Brar, meanwhile, wasn’t part of the original Test squad. But after being adjudged Player of the Series in the ODIs, he was added to the Test party in place of leftarm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.Can India turn back to the experience and inexhaustible energy of Mohammed Siraj in place of Akash Deep? That relentless intensity was something India missed at the Basin once the pitch flattened.The current regime under Gill and coach Gautam Gambhir has prioritised current form and the eye test in the nets. By the looks of it, Siraj hasn’t quite passed that test yet, despite Gill speaking glowingly about him in Wellington.But if Gill and Gambhir care for history, someone could perhaps point them towards one striking statistic. India have won nine Tests in SENA countries since 2020 and Siraj has featured in every one of them, playing significant roles along the way.Hagley, like the Basin, has a reputation for rewarding seam, with its grass cover offering the quicks assistance over the first couple of days before batting tends to become easier, particularly under bright skies. The forecast suggests sunshine over the first three days, but considerably more cloud and rain on Days Four and Five. That could make having fresh legs in the pace attack even more important.India were handed first use of the Basin pitch after winning the toss and reduced New Zealand to 70/5. At Hagley, should they win the toss again, expect them to have no hesitation in inserting New Zealand.History backs that instinct too: in the 15 Tests played here, teams winning the toss and choosing to bowl first have gone on to win nine times.With valuable World Test Championship points available before New Zealand head across the Tasman to face Australia and India prepare to host Australia for five Tests, both teams will desperately want a result.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Everyone who gave me grief': Ben Stokes' cheeky take on Shubman Gill ending 1st IND vs NZ Test early evokes Manchester memories
articles.summary: Ben Stokes took a cheeky swipe at his critics after Shubman Gill's decision to end the first India vs New Zealand Test early brought back memories of Manches...
articles.body:
Ben Stokes revisited the Manchester handshake controversy after the first India vs New Zealand Test ended early.

He noted Shubman Gill's concern over Daryl Mitchell being on 49 before the batter initiated the handshake.

The former England captain cheekily hit back at critics of his own early handshake against India in 2025.

What did Ben Stokes say about Shubman Gill's handshake against New Zealand?

India vs New Zealand Test match in Wellington saw an early draw, reminding people of the 2025 Manchester Test, where Ben Stokes was criticised by many for handing India an early handshake.

A post on Instagram regarding the current situation indicated that Ben would be happy with how things went down.

"Really like how Gill actually thought Mitchell is on 49 and might not shake hands but Mitchell just came forward himself. Ben Stokes would be happy," the post said.

Discussing the issue in an episode of That's Not Cricket , Ben explained that Gill seemed afraid that Mitchell wouldn't shake hands while scoring 49 runs and then stepped forward of his own accord, ending the game at 239/5.

"There was a lot of debate around that and I think this is now in front of me because what's happened is Shubman Gill of the Indian cricket team are in a position that we were as a team there in a result that was going to be a draw."

He continued, "And he was hoping that the opposition would shake hands so he could get his team off the field. But he thinks that someone being on 49, close to a landmark, means that they are not going to."

"Can we just say that everyone who reacted gave me a little grief. Can we get a reaction to Shubman Gill shaking hands and Daryl Mitchell doing the right thing by shaking hands when there cannot be a result? Thanks, Daryl."

What happened during the first India vs New Zealand Test in Wellington?

India and New Zealand shared an interesting draw in the first Test match held at the Basin Reserve, Wellington.

India had got themselves into a dominant position after declaring at 720/9. However, the gritty performance from the New Zealand batters ensured that India did not get anything out of the match.

New Zealand ended up at 239/5 with Daryl Mitchell being not out for 49 and Glenn Phillips at 26 when the decision to conclude the match was taken.

Gill's decision to shake hands with the opposition came while around 15 overs were still left in the day. The skipper explained his move by saying that his fast bowlers would be getting a lot of workload.

Why did Ben Stokes face criticism during the 2025 Manchester Test?

This was reminiscent of the fourth England against India Test at Old Trafford played in July 2025, where Stokes extended an early handshake with 15 overs left in the game.

But Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar did not extend their hands in reciprocation, as they approached the century mark in their respective innings, scoring 89 runs and 80 runs respectively.

The two put on an unbeaten stand of 203 runs before declaring the innings at 425/4. It turned out to be a draw for the match.

The gesture of the England skipper led to heated arguments as to whether he was right in calling off the match even though there were personal goals to be scored by the opposition team members.

The Cricket News Opinion: Stokes gets his moment of vindication

Stokes' action can be forgiven considering the criticism he got after the Manchester Test. He was in the same predicament but with no hope of a result, whereas the Indian team decided to keep on batting.

The incident in Wellington provided a funny comparison. It seemed like Gill thought about whether Mitchell was ready to complete his half-century before making his move, but Mitchell came forward to shake hands.

Neither Gill nor Mitchell can be blamed because the captains have to think about the match situation as well as the chances of getting a result when deciding to end the game.

Nevertheless, Stokes was glad that he could make a comparison between their actions because he was criticised for his offer in Manchester.

articles.title: IPL 2027 mini-auction: Remaining purse and budget for each Indian Premier League team detailed
articles.summary: Check the remaining purse and auction budget for all 10 teams ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction in Goa, including the ₹157 crore salary cap and trade impact...
articles.body:
Franchises have swapped several big names in recent months.

One blockbuster exchange involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh stands out among the deals.

Purse sizes differ sharply across the ten teams before the mini-auction.

IPL 2027 auction purse remaining: Team-by-team budget breakdown after retention lists and deadline-day trades

With the IPL 2027 mini-auction on the horizon, every franchise is keeping a close watch on how much money it has left to spend.

Over the last few months, a good number of players have moved between teams through trades, many of them seeking a better role or more game time at their new teams. Some of these deals were straight swaps, while one was completed as a cash transaction.

The biggest name to change hands is Hardik Pandya, who has gone from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore. Arshdeep Singh has travelled in the opposite direction at the same price, which means the two sides have effectively exchanged one star for another.

Rishabh Pant's return to Delhi Capitals for Rs 15 crore, with Kuldeep Yadav heading to Lucknow Super Giants at Rs 13.50 crore, is another marquee trade deal.

Harshal Patel's move from Sunrisers to Gujarat Titans for Rs 4 crore was the only cash deal on the list, and Rajasthan Royals added Mohammed Shami and Manimaran Siddharth from Lucknow in return for Sam Curran.

Retention list: CSK | MI | RCB | KKR | RR | SRH | PBKS | DC | LSG | GT

IPL 2027 auction purse details for all teams

How is the purse amount determined for each team?

Every franchise had the original purse of 120 crore ahead of last year's mega auction, through which they built their roster for the 2025-27 cycle.

Before each mini-auction, INR 5 crore is added to the purse, so teams in Goa on December 16 will be operating with a maximum of IR 130 crore (includes salary for retained players as well).

The IPL 2027 mini-auction will take place on Wednesday, December 16, 2026, in Goa, India.

The 10 franchises will have an opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players from the auction pool.

The auction follows the November 17 retention deadline, when franchises submitted their final lists of retained and released players to the BCCI ahead of the event.

Meanwhile, the trade deadline continues until a week before the auction (December 9).

articles.title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack.Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus.Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format.Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket.Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approachSooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers.Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir."We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel."The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added.'This is another level'Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it."What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said.Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle."I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Rajasthan Royals missed a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to acquire Hardik Pandya
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ever since Mumbai Indians (MI) played their last league match of IPL 2026, speculation was rife over Hardik Pandya's future.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ever since Mumbai Indians (MI) played their last league match of IPL 2026, speculation was rife over Hardik Pandya's future. Multiple teams were in the race to sign the flamboyant all-rounder, whose second stint with MI, having returned to the franchise in the 2024 season as captain, replacing long-serving skipper Rohit Sharma, didn't go as planned. The five-time IPL champions failed to qualify for the playoffs twice in the three seasons since Pandya took over the captaincy.Rajasthan Royals (RR), the inaugural champions of the IPL, were in the driver's seat to acquire Hardik. The Royals' owners and their Director of Cricket, Kumar Sangakkara, flew all the way to Bengaluru to sign the deal.However, it's understood that the trade fell through when MI asked to include England pacer Jofra Archer along with opener Yashasvi Jaiswal in the deal. MI were clear that they would trade Hardik to Rajasthan only if they agreed to include Archer in the deal. But Rajasthan Royals opted against it.Would that have been a setback for the Royals? Not necessarily. They would have acquired the services of India's No. 1 all-rounder and a captain. Now, after this failed trade, RR will have to continue with the options they have. Riyan Parag is now set to lead the Rajasthan Royals in the IPL 2027 season.Under Riyan, the Royals qualified for the playoffs in IPL 2026 but his own form was underwhelming as he struggled with the bat. The Royals now have no choice but to continue with him, who, as a player, is yet to establish himself in the Indian cricket team.In Hardik, the Royals could have signed a proven championship-winning captain, something they have lacked for years. Hardik had led Gujarat Titans (GT) to the title in their debut season in 2022. GT also reached the final in 2023. Around Hardik and with the pot of gold they have unearthed in Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Royals missed a chance to build a championship-winning side.Despite the fitness concerns, Hardik remains a force to reckon with as a player, and the numbers don't lie. Across 162 IPL matches, he has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and claimed 82 wickets, underlining his value as a proven match-winner.Rajasthan Royals' loss proved to be Punjab Kings' gain, who didn't even hesitate to trade their premier pacer Arshdeep Singh to sign Hardik Pandya in one of the biggest and most high-profile player exchanges in IPL history.Hardik Pandya moved to Punjab Kings from Mumbai Indians at an increased fee of Rs 18 crore (Pandya’s existing fee was Rs 16.35 crore). Arshdeep, on the other hand, moved to Mumbai at an unchanged price tag of Rs 18 crore.Hardik’s trade brought the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles. Having first joined MI in 2015, the 33-year-old had starring roles with both bat and ball during the team’s title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. Alas, it didn't end on a high.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Nvidia AI chips in Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's bat': Iceland Cricket's post on 15-year-old goes viral
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's stunning double-century against the UAE has taken the cricket world by surprise.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's stunning double-century against the UAE has taken the cricket world by surprise. The 15-year-old smashed 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, leaving fans and former cricketers amazed.Even Iceland Cricket joined the conversation with a hilarious post on social media, bringing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang into the discussion. The cricket board joked that Sooryavanshi's bat was powered by artificial intelligence (AI) chips."It's no coincidence that on Tuesday Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO and on Wednesday, the AI chips in Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's bat came back," Iceland Cricket posted on X.Sooryavanshi's innings included 28 sixes and helped him break several records in List A cricket. He now holds the record for the fastest double-century in the format, reaching the 200-run mark in just 52 balls.Sooryavanshi rewrites List A recordsThe young left-hander's knock was special not just because of the number of runs he scored but also because of the speed at which he reached the milestones.Here are some of the records created by Sooryavanshi:Fastest double-centuries in List A cricket: Sooryavanshi reached 200 in 52 balls against the UAE in 2026. Chad Bowes is second on the list with a 103-ball double-century for Canterbury against Otago in 2024. N Jagadeesan and Harry Brook have also scored double-centuries in 114 balls.Most sixes in a professional cricket innings: Sooryavanshi's 28 sixes are now the most in all professional cricket. Tanmay Agarwal is second with 26 sixes for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy in 2024.Most sixes in a List A innings: Sooryavanshi leads the list with 28 sixes. D'Arcy Short had hit 23 for Western Australia against Queensland in 2018, while Bevon Jacobs struck 21 for Auckland against Otago in 2026.His 28-ball century and his 150-run milestone were also the fastest in List A cricket. The 150-run mark broke a record that Sooryavanshi himself had previously held. His strike rate of 384.90 is also the highest recorded for a List A century.Yuvraj Singh's advice helped Sooryavanshi bounce backAfter his record-breaking performance, Sooryavanshi revealed that a half-hour conversation with former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh helped him overcome a difficult period and regain his confidence.The youngster said he spoke to four people before the match against the UAE, including his father, childhood coach Manish Ojha, friend Pratham Jachak and Yuvraj."I spoke to only four people (before going into the match). Of course, I spoke to my father. Then my childhood coach, Manish Ojha and my friend, who was with me from the Under-19s - his name is Pratham Jachak. The fourth one is Yuvraj (Singh) sir. I spoke to him for almost half-an-hour," Sooryavanshi said in a video posted on bcci.tv. on Wednesday.Yuvraj has also guided young Indian batters such as Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill. Sooryavanshi said he openly discussed the problems he was facing with his batting, and the former India all-rounder gave him technical advice."He explained a lot of things about my batting. Because I was very tense, I spoke to him openly. 'Sir, I am having these problems when I am going out to bat'. He explained everything to me for half an hour. He mainly told me, 'If you bat for 20 balls, the team's score will be different'. He told me a lot of technical things. All of that helped me a lot."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant took part in a local cricket match in Christchurch on Wednesday, using the opportunity to to keep his eye sharp
articles.body: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant took part in a local cricket match in Christchurch on Wednesday, using the opportunity to to keep his eye sharp ahead of the second New Zealand Test starting Friday.Pant, 29, is one of the leading six-hitters in Test cricket history. He has hit 108 sixes in 53 matches, the second-highest tally in the format.Six of those sixes came in the first Test in Wellington last week, where his 128 off 153 balls helped India post a record total of 720/9 in New Zealand. The match ended in a draw.Pant's appearance in a local Last Man Stands match came after he was spotted in central Christchurch.One team, Open House Swingers, were down a player and asked Pant if he would fill in, with the Indian star wasting no time picking up the bat to give them a boost.He turned out for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park. The venue is next to Hagley Oval, where he will represent India in the second Test.Listed as Stan Stan on the scorecard, Pant scored 54 off 21 balls, continuing his run-scoring form in New Zealand."I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike," Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald."So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us?"He was like, OK, I'll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes."India bowling coach Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that".New Zealand captain Tom Latham described Pant's performance as "brilliant"."He's obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it's great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams."Safi told the New Zealand Herald that the opposition players did not recognise Pant, who was wearing a blue tracksuit. He also said Pant had used his cousin's bat during the match."He was asking me to basically give him a single and stuff. Obviously, I was smashing longer sixes than him, and then he was like, give me a turn, let me show you how to hit it," Safi said.The Open House Swingers won the match by 16 runs.India's second Test against New Zealand begins on Friday at Hagley Oval.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Audition at India nets: Gurnoor Brar turns up the heat in wet and chilly Christchurch
articles.summary: CHRISTCHURCH: India's only net session before the second Test against New Zealand was turning out to be quite a dampener because of relentless rain.
articles.body: CHRISTCHURCH: India's only net session before the second Test against New Zealand was turning out to be quite a dampener because of relentless rain. The team reached Hagley Oval amidst steady drizzle, and the first batch, KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dhruv Jurel, was forced to hit the AstroTurf in the indoor nets. There wasn't much to do, and the side-armers allowed the batters to get a feel for the ball before the skies above cleared to make way for some sunshine. The ground staff turned the training square around in miraculous time, and the players were able to get a proper hit before the final game of the tour.Away from the group, bowlers Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna were in the main ground doing release work. The bowling pack was the centre of attention as it was the only department India are likely to tinker with for the must-win clash. Bowling coach Morne Morkel didn't offer any hints, but there were enough cues from the nets to convey the strong possibility of Gurnoor Brar making his Test debut.Gurnoor Brar is a guy who will be well-suited to the conditions here.He operated with a lot of heat against captain Shubman Gill, and while it's unusual for a fast bowler to run in with that intensity on the eve of the match, Brar was probably showing his rhythm. A short burst later, he was asked to take it easy, and a short conversation followed between captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir. Minutes later, Gambhir had a few words for the young bowler, who rushed to pad up for a decent hit.Interestingly, he was the only bowler from the entire squad to get some batting done and was closely watched by Gambhir. With the pitch expected to ease out for batting as the game progresses, the think tank is strongly pondering adding a few more yards to their attack. When asked about Brar's readiness, Morkel asserted that he is good to go and will be ideal for these conditions."There's a lot of excitement about him since he joined the Indian team because of his pace and bounce. He's a guy that will be well-suited to the conditions here. So, yeah, we'll see how it goes. He is knocking on the door, he is doing the right things. He has the bounce, pace and skill, and these conditions would suit him," said Morkel without revealing much about the Playing XI."He needs to just make sure he's ready when he gets the opportunity. I think a lot of times, we think we want that opportunity. We want to be close, and as a bowler, you can get distracted. When he gets his opportunity, which is... You know, we never know. My job is to make sure he's 100% ready when he gets that opportunity," he further added.India persisted with Prasidh Krishna as their only tall fast bowler for the series opener, but the returns were far from encouraging in the first innings. He failed to pose any major threat on the "lifeless pitch", and even though the reading improved in the second innings, it doesn't reveal the entire story. Prasidh was economical, bowled 10 maidens, but the spell came at a time when the opposition pair of Darryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips was happy to eat time and never looked like scoring.With both Kamboj and Akash offering value with the bat, and the team's obsession with depth, the only change likely at this stage is Brar coming in for Prasidh. There could be a late twist in the selection tale depending on what they make of the pitch on the morning of the game, but the cues on match eve didn't point in that direction.In Brar, Gill would get an attacking bowler in good form, with the ability to operate in the higher 140s. Pace has been captain Gill's obsession, and he now has the opportunity to unleash the bowler he has been grooming for the role which the team badly wants him to perform.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Deny until you die': Now, Ben Stokes takes aim at Sandpapergate as row spills over
articles.summary: Former England captain Ben Stokes has urged Australian players involved in the Sandpapergate controversy to stop their public exchanges, saying the
articles.body: Former England captain Ben Stokes has urged Australian players involved in the Sandpapergate controversy to stop their public exchanges, saying the renewed debate is affecting people beyond those who took part in the incident.The ball-tampering scandal, which took place during Australia's 2018 Test series in South Africa, has returned to the spotlight 8 1/2 years later following the publication of former opener Usman Khawaja's autobiography. The latest revelations have once again divided Australian cricket, with players offering conflicting accounts of what happened.“For the sake of players, the staff, the management who were involved in this whole situation, for the sake of their families, for the sake of their friends, the best thing for it to do now would be for it just to just to stop,” Stokes said on his “That's Not Cricket” podcast on Wednesday. “It’s affecting people who do not deserve to be affected by this.”Stokes' comments carry significance given the rivalry between England and Australia, two of cricket's oldest opponents. The teams will mark 150 years since their first Test match next March.Stokes played a key role for England over a 15-year international career, which included World Cup titles in the 50-over and T20 formats, performances that became part of Ashes history and his captaincy during the Bazball era.He has also been involved in incidents away from cricket that attracted media attention. Stokes was found not guilty of affray (assault) in 2018 following a late-night street fight in Bristol, southwest England, after England's win over the West Indies. He was also dropped for a match against New Zealand following a nightclub incident in June. He returned to the team before announcing his sudden retirement.Speaking about the impact of Sandpapergate, Stokes said the controversy had affected more than just the players involved.“Because I’ve been through something like this when you are so heavily in the media for something, I’ve seen what it’s done to people who don’t deserve to be put through stress, put through anxiety,” Stokes said. “Whoever was in charge of Cricket Australia at the time have a lot to answer for this.”The latest debate has seen players and members of the support staff involved in the 2018 South Africa Test series offer different versions of events. Three Australian players were handed bans after the ball-tampering incident, but Khawaja has written in his autobiography that the entire team knew about the plan and should have accepted collective responsibility.Current Australia captain Pat Cummins is among those who have denied knowing about the plan.“It’s got so deep into it ... that it’s almost just like ‘deny until you die’ one way or the other,” Stokes said. “I’ve been in the dressing room for long enough to form my own very well educated guess on what I think has happened, but I don’t think in the close future we're going to hear what truly happened because it’s just so deep.”Meanwhile, Cricket Australia has backed Cummins to continue as Test captain ahead of next month's series against New Zealand. The decision has ended speculation over his position amid the conflicting accounts of what he knew during the 2018 South Africa series.Cricket Australia chairman David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg issued a statement on Cummins' captaincy after the board announced that players from the 2018 series would be invited to take part in an independent forum and share their accounts of the incident.Cummins took over as Test captain from Tim Paine in late 2021. Paine had been appointed to the role in the aftermath of Sandpapergate.Steve Smith and David Warner, who were Australia's captain and vice-captain during the 2018 series, were banned for 12 months by Cricket Australia following the public reaction to the scandal. Cameron Bancroft, who was caught on television footage with sandpaper, received a nine-month suspension.Cummins' account of the incident has been challenged by Bancroft and Warner.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Hundred to introduce semi-finals from 2027
articles.summary: An extra match will be added to The Hundred for the first time in 2027 with the introduction of four-team semi-finals.
articles.body:
An extra match will be added to The Hundred for the first time in 2027 with the introduction of semi-finals.

In the previous six editions of The Hundred, only the top three qualified from the eight-team group stage. First place went straight to the final, with second and third playing in the eliminator.

Now, the top four will play in traditional semis in a move designed to increase the competitiveness of the group stage and create an extra marquee fixture.

The Hundred window will not be expanded to accommodate the semi-finals – the competition will still be completed in just under four weeks.

Instead, finals weekend will be altered. In 2026, for the first time, a reserve day was scheduled for the eliminator, which was played on a Friday before the final took place on a Sunday.

In 2027, the semi-finals will take place on Friday and Saturday, followed by the Sunday final.

The Oval has become the regular venue for the eliminator, with Lord's hosting the final. Having both games in London has minimised travel for the teams having to play an extra game to reach the final.

In the new structure, The Oval is expected to host the Saturday semi-final. The venue for the first semi is to be confirmed.

The tweak in the format of The Hundred comes a year after investors began to exert influence over the eight franchises.

In 2025, the England and Wales Cricket Board sold stakes in all eight franchises, raising more than £500m to be distributed across the game. Investors became involved in the running of their teams ahead of the 2026 season.

The move to introduce a second semi-final has not been directly influenced by the arrival of external investment, though it has been welcomed by owners.

A primary motivation has come from a desire to maximise the competitiveness of matches played in the latter stage of the group phase.

The Hundred group stage is relatively short – only eight matches per team – meaning the margin between qualifying or missing out on the play-offs can be thin.

In the 2026 men's competition, fourth-placed MI London finished on the same points as Sunrisers Leeds in third. On the women's side, Manchester Super Giants finished fourth, two points behind Southern Brave, yet Super Giants were one of only two teams to have a match abandoned because of the weather.

The 2027 Hundred is set to begin on 3 August, the day after the scheduled fifth day of the final Ashes Test between England and Australia at The Oval. The Hundred finals day will be held on 29 August.

Trent Rockets are the defending women's champions, while Manchester Super Giants are holders of the men's title.

articles.title: 102 matches, over five-thousand runs: Former India U19 World Cup winner quits first-class cricket at 32
articles.summary: Former India Under-19 World Cup-winning all-rounder Baba Aparajith has retired from first-class cricket at the age of 32, ending a career in which he
articles.body: Former India Under-19 World Cup-winning all-rounder Baba Aparajith has retired from first-class cricket at the age of 32, ending a career in which he represented Tamil Nadu, Kerala and India A, besides being part of Chennai Super Kings and Rising Pune Supergiant in the IPL.Aparajith announced his retirement through an Instagram post on Wednesday, revealing that his last first-class match was played on January 24, 2026."I played my last first-class cricket match on January 24, 2026, officially bringing my first-class cricketing career to a close. Looking back, it has been an incredible journey filled with experiences, challenges, lessons, friendships and memories that I will cherish for a lifetime. It has been an absolute privilege to represent Tamil Nadu, India Under-19, India A, Kerala, Chennai Super Kings, Rising Pune Supergiant, TNPL franchises and my club teams, and to be part of the many teams and dressing rooms that have shaped my journey. Each experience has played a significant role in shaping me, both as a cricketer and as a person," he wrote on Instagram.Aparajith was part of India's Under-19 World Cup-winning team in 2012. He scored 171 runs and took five wickets during the tournament, finishing as India's fourth-highest run-scorer. He also won the Man-of-the-Match award in the quarter-final against Pakistan Under-19s and the semi-final against New Zealand Under-19s.The batting all-rounder made his Ranji Trophy debut for Tamil Nadu at the age of 17 before representing India Under-19s at the World Cup in Australia in 2012. He later broke into the India A setup in 2015 but could not establish himself consistently at that level.Aparajith was part of Chennai Super Kings for three consecutive seasons between 2013 and 2015 but never made his IPL debut for the franchise. He was also part of Rising Pune Supergiant in the league. However, he was largely viewed as an accumulator, with his overall strike rate of 108 across 63 T20 matches reflecting his batting approach.He played 102 first-class matches, most of them for Tamil Nadu, scoring 12 centuries and 27 half-centuries. He also contributed with his off-spin and had the opportunity to captain Tamil Nadu.Aparajith was part of three title-winning Tamil Nadu squads, winning the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2017-18 and the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in 2020-21 and 2021-22. He also represented Kerala during the final phase of his domestic career.Aparajith, whose twin brother Baba Indrajith is also a cricketer, thanked the cricketing bodies, his family, coaches, teammates and support staff for their backing throughout his career."My sincere gratitude to the BCCI, TNCA and KCA for the opportunities and support throughout my career. A special mention to my wife, my parents, my brother, my extended family, and all my friends and well-wishers for their unconditional support, sacrifices and belief in me throughout this journey. I’m grateful to my coaches, support staff and teammates who have been an integral part of this journey. My connection with the game will remain as strong as ever. I look forward to carrying forward the knowledge, experiences and lessons gathered over the years, continuing to learn, contribute and hopefully make a meaningful impact on the game in the years ahead," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ben Stokes on the Ashes, Joe Root and Stephen Fleming's new era in charge of the England Test team
articles.summary: "I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at," Stokes told Sky Sports, adding: "I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well"
articles.body:
Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of the launch of a new podcast he's presenting with Mark Wood called 'That's Not Cricket', Stokes admitted his surprise that Joe Root succeeded him as Test captain but offered him full support ahead of next summer's series against Australia.

England's Test team enter into a new era under Root - who returned to the captaincy with a 3-0 series sweep of Pakistan following Stokes' international retirement - and Fleming, who begins as head coach with a three-Test tour of South Africa next month.

The series, against the reigning World Test Champions, serves as an ideal challenge for the new regime as they steel themselves for the visit of Australia next summer where they'll look to regain the Ashes for the first time since winning on home soil in 2015.

"I'm doing a Glenn McGrath here; I hope England win the Ashes 5-0," Stokes said. "I'm not saying they will, but I wish nothing but the best for them.

"I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well.

"There is no animosity whatsoever between any of us, there's no jealousy."

Stokes did add, however, that he was "surprised" to see Root take on the captaincy again, knowing first-hand how much the job takes out of you - as well as the toll it had taken on Root by the time he handed over the reins in 2022 after five years in the role.

"I was a little bit surprised, if I'm being honest, just because he knows what it's like and he's done so well as a player but also, knowing Joe, he feels like he can take the team from where it was and build on it again," Stokes said.

"It's an exciting time for someone to think like that and when Stephen Fleming got appointed , I thought 'these two are going to work really well together'.

"I did a lot of work with Flem in the IPL. He's a great man manager; everyone has already seen how he speaks , which is very impressive. I'm excited to watch them go about it."

Stokes: Everything after Ashes defeat was tough

Stokes' time as Test captain and as an England cricketer came to an end with a 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand, which was on the heels of a disastrous 4-1 Ashes drubbing in Australia during the winter.

"I was in the right headspace for the Ashes," Stokes reflected. "It was all after that. Before the Ashes, I was so confident.

"Everyone was fit, firing and ready to go. Fans and pundits were all confident, and Australia weren't confident, so we couldn't have been in a better place going out there.

"But emotion and the feeling of what you think is going to happen is completely different to getting out there in the heat of the battle. Everything after that was tough."

Stokes added: "Unfortunately, to do that role, you have to immerse yourself in it, have to throw yourself into it.

"For all the positive stuff that comes with it, there is a negative effect that can flow over into your home life and your family.

"I think every England captain will have that. I don't think there is anything you can do.

"You can try your hardest, but when you do that role you just have to do it. I don't think you are doing the role justice if you take it lightly.

"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at."

As well as still playing for his county side Durham - helping them clinch promotion back to Division One of the County Championship - and an upcoming stint with the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League, Stokes is using his newfound freedom to venture into the world of podcasting.

"I have been in the public eye for so long but people who don't know me probably only know 10, 15, 20 per cent of what I am actually like," he said. "That is the exciting thing: I now get a chance to say what I want to be going out.

"I don't feel like you're always necessarily able to give that full account of yourself as a person, because you're wary of upsetting people. The only person I can upset now is myself.

"It's really exciting and I can't wait to get going. We've got a lot to talk about and a lot to say."

Sandpapergate is 'far beyond' England issues

Stokes would not be drawn on Sandpapergate or the possibility of him making a comeback for the Ashes, hinting he would save that for his new podcast.

He spoke about the saga dominating Australian cricket on the first episode, which was released on Wednesday, and told Sky Sports how hard it would be to handle.

"It's all kicking off at the moment out there, isn't it?," he said.

"What Australia have going on there is far beyond anything we had to deal with [as a leadership group].

"I imagine Joe [Root] and Flem [Stephen Fleming] would be thinking, 'imagine if this happened three weeks before the Ashes next year, as opposed to now'."

articles.title: 'Vaibhav can chase 450 on last day of a Test': 'Effective' Sooryavanshi backed for red-ball cricket
articles.summary: New Zealand leg-spinner Ish Sodhi believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the ability to succeed in Test cricket, pointing to the teenager's batting technique
articles.body: New Zealand leg-spinner Ish Sodhi believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the ability to succeed in Test cricket, pointing to the teenager's batting technique and ability to hit the ball across the ground.Sooryavanshi has drawn attention with his performances, including his recent record-breaking 53-ball double century against UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup.“I haven’t seen anyone in my career strike the ball as consistently as he does. He is a phenomenal left-hand batter."“Along with Abhishek Sharma, he provides huge power for India moving forward," Sodhi said, as quoted by news agency PTI.Sodhi was also asked whether Sooryavanshi could make the transition to red-ball cricket. The New Zealand spinner felt the youngster's attacking approach could be useful in Test matches, particularly when teams are chasing big totals in the fourth innings on pitches that offer little assistance to bowlers.“I had this conversation with someone the other day. Can he be a red-ball player? I think his fundamentals are phenomenal. The way he strikes the ball in all areas of the park, his technique is surely good enough.“I was thinking, if you play a Test match and have 380 or 400 to chase on the last day, someone like him would be unbelievable to have in your side.“Predominantly at Hagley Oval, it gets quite flat in the fourth innings, and it would be tough for opposition attacks to keep him quiet.”However, Sodhi said there were still questions about Sooryavanshi's ability to bat for long periods and defend consistently, aspects of the game that are important in Test cricket.“If we look at it in the traditional sense, can he bat for really long periods? Can he occupy time at the crease? I’m not sure. I haven’t seen his defensive technique a lot.“But can he be effective in Test cricket? Absolutely,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tom Banton handed England captaincy for T20I series finale against Australia and left 'emotional' by brief promotion
articles.summary: Tom Banton will replace Harry Brook as captain for Wednesday's fifth T20I against Australia, with Brook heading home and Will Jacks out injured; England face matches on Friday (Brisbane) and Sunday (Sydney) before the series finale in Canberra
articles.body:
White-ball captain Harry Brook is flying home before the fifth and final T20 against Australia next Wednesday, while regular deputy Will Jacks has been ruled out of the rest of the series due to a broken hand.

Banton will become just the 14th player to captain England in a T20I, with the 28-year-old first told by head coach Brendon McCullum as the team prepared to board a flight in Melbourne last week.

"I was pretty emotional when I got told a few days ago in the airport," Banton told reporters ahead of Friday's third T20I, with the series currently tied 1-1. "Baz [McCullum] just pulled me aside and told me.

"I didn't know how to react if I'm honest, to be told you will captain your country is a huge privilege. It's a great honour, a great privilege and something I'm looking forward to.

"It was a strange feeling when I first got told, and something I've been thinking a lot about over the last few days. But I don't want things to change a lot, I'm just going to try and follow what Brooky and the guys have been doing so well in the last year or two."

The promotion shows his growth in stature in international cricket, having first been selected aged 20 before having nearly three and a half years away from England ahead of last summer's recall.

Banton said he "hated cricket" during that period but has since rediscovered his love for the sport, making a strong case to open the batting at next year's ODI World Cup and carving out a spot in the middle order of the T20 side.

"It was a weird time in my career, those few years," Banton added. "I learned a lot about myself and it put me in the position I'm in today,"

Opener Phil Salt was among the other captaincy options, having led the side against Australia in 2024 - when Banton was not even part of the squad.

Brook ready to return to 'special' Gabba

There are two games to play before Banton formally becomes an England skipper, with the visitors facing Australia in Brisbane on Friday and Sydney on Sunday before he replaces Brook in Canberra.

The Gabba has seen many painful chapters for English Ashes hopes over the years, from Nasser Hussain's fateful decision to bowl first in 2002 to Steve Harmison's wide to second slip four years later, while the venue was also where England were beaten during last year's Ashes defeat.

Brook is the only current squad member who was involved in that trip, but Banton has much happier memories of the notoriously hostile venue having played for Brisbane Heat in two seasons of the Big Bash League.

"I was lucky enough to play here a few times for the Heat, so it does have a bit of a special place in my heart," Brook said. "They gave me my first opportunity to play franchise cricket so I'll be forever thankful to them and to everyone here.

"I just walked past the overseas player board and saw it was 2019. It was a great time in my life and I look back on it with fond memories."

articles.title: Ireland to make historic first-ever tour of Pakistan, six-match series confirmed
articles.summary: Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in
articles.body: Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in Lahore as part of their preparations for the ICC World Cup Qualifier.Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore.The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The matches will be played on January 13, 15 and 17 against the Shaheens, before the two teams meet in the ODIs on January 20, 22 and 24. Match timings are yet to be confirmed.While this will be the first visit to Pakistan by the Ireland men's side, it will not be the first tour by an Irish cricket team. The Ireland women's side visited the country in 2022 and famously won the T20I series.World Cup Qualifier preparations behind Ireland's tourThe six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February 2027, which will be held in South Africa and Namibia.Graeme West, Cricket Ireland's Director of High Performance, underlined the importance of the tour in providing the one-day squad with valuable match practice ahead of the qualification campaign.“This is an extremely important tour for our One-Day squad as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifiers in February. Following the nine games played in the second half of 2026, a further six 50-over matches against quality opponents will support the players readiness for the qualifier taking place in South Africa and Namibia.“While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027.“Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope.”The Pakistan Cricket Board had initially planned a triangular series involving Ireland, Pakistan and Zimbabwe. However, Zimbabwe subsequently withdrew, citing its inability to travel to Pakistan. The revised arrangement will see Ireland play two separate three-match assignments instead.Ireland-Pakistan ODI rivalryIreland and Pakistan have faced each other seven times in men's ODIs, with Pakistan winning five matches, Ireland claiming one victory and one encounter ending in a tie.Ireland's only win remains one of the most memorable results in its cricketing history. It came during the 2007 World Cup in the Caribbean, when Ireland stunned Pakistan to knock the former champions out of the tournament.Pakistan, meanwhile, will enter the series after winning the ODI tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and Lahore last month, under the captaincy of Shaheen Shah Afridi.The six-match series will also offer Pakistan valuable preparation ahead of its international assignments in 2027, including the ODI World Cup later in the year.Pakistan vs Ireland Fixtures13 January: Ireland Men v Shaheens – 1st 50-over match (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)15 January: Ireland Men v Shaheens – 2nd 50-over match (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)17 January: Ireland Men v Shaheens – 3rd 50-over match (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)20 January: Ireland Men v Pakistan Men – 1st ODI (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)22 January: Ireland Men v Pakistan Men – 2nd ODI (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)24 January: Ireland Men v Pakistan Men – 3rd ODI (Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Captain is the main man': On nostalgic night, John Wright delivers message for the present
articles.summary: CHRISTCHURCH: \"Captain is the main man,\" says John Wright, recalling his time as head coach of the Indian cricket team and his successful partnership with
articles.body: CHRISTCHURCH: "Captain is the main man," says John Wright, recalling his time as head coach of the Indian cricket team and his successful partnership with Sourav Ganguly. At an event celebrating 100 years of unity through sport, Wright spoke about leaving Anil Kumble out of the 2003 World Cup final and experimenting with Virender Sehwag at the top of the order. Yet, the conversation never revolved around him. It remained focused on Sourav, the leader, the captain and the man who truly shaped Indian cricket in the early 2000s.With Hagley Oval in the backdrop, Wright recalled his early days at the historic venue. He looked forward to the upcoming Test between India and New Zealand with a lot of excitement. This Test presents Shubman Gill with an opportunity to embody Wright's "main man" talk and allows the young captain to stamp his leadership authority.Indian cricket has often seen captains who pick their coaches, but with Gill, it was the other way around. He became the unanimous choice of head coach Gautam Gambhir, then chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar and other influential figures in Indian cricket after Rohit Sharma decided to move on from Test cricket. Since then, Gill has been taking baby steps into the leadership role but is yet to stamp the kind of authority his predecessors had.Gill's bat has been on fire with the captain's armband, but it's time he starts shaping the team as his own rather than getting overburdened by the coach's ideologies. Gambhir's contract lasts until the end of the 2027 ODI World Cup, but Gill, 27, is certainly here to stay, both as a captain and a cricketer. It's time the team and tactics start looking like an extension of the captain's mindset and ideologies, not the coach's.It's no longer a secret that coach Gambhir is obsessed with left-right combinations, batting depth and utility players. But can the same be said about Gill? Not really.For now, the only clear aspect of Gill's captaincy template is his preference for tall fast bowlers who can hit the deck hard and maintain pace during long spells. He has now led India in five Tests against England, two against the West Indies, one against South Africa (where he retired hurt midway), two against Sri Lanka and the ongoing two-Test series against New Zealand.With 11 Tests completed and the 12th approaching, by the time the New Zealand tour ends, Gill should establish himself as the strongest and loudest voice in the changeroom. The sample size is now big enough to establish patterns, trends and preferences. Even if the ongoing World Test Championship cycle ship has sailed, the next one remains important. Not just for Gill the captain and leader, but also for Indian cricket.I'll tell you what, all these guys want to play in that (WTC) final, and they'll give everything possible to make it. But realistically, if we're honest, it's going to be a challenge.The unanimous word from the Indian dressing room has been how badly they want to play in the World Test Championship final next year, but the talk hasn't really translated into action. The series defeat to South Africa at home severely hurt their chances, and the draws in Colombo and Wellington have further pushed them back."I'll tell you what, all these guys want to play in that (WTC) final, and they'll give everything possible to make it. But realistically, if we're honest, it's going to be a challenge," Team India's bowling coach Morne Morkel told reporters on the eve of the second Test.Morne Morkel was straightforward, offering the first realistic assessment from the dressing room on the WTC final. No matter how optimistic we sound and rely on mathematical calculations, the dream is no longer alive.But what remains alive is captain Gill's quest for glory and Indian cricket's wait for its young leader to stamp his authority and make this team his own.Just like the wonder boys of the 2000s, which remained Ganguly's team, with Wright happy to be the co-passenger. The veteran coach fondly remembers his boys, who are all now taking a plunge into IPL coaching, but for him, Sourav remains the real deal."Yuvi (Yuvraj Singh) will be with Sourav at Delhi Capitals, Zaheer Khan is with CSK and L Balaji with the India A team now. But Sourav is Sourav," he chuckles.Even in the chuckle remembering the past, a message for India's present lay there.Gill, the leader, and not Gambhir, the coach, matters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Punjab Kings (PBKS) will need to make the right bowling acquisitions at the upcoming IPL auction if they are to end their long wait for a maiden title in 2027, according to former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara. While the arrival of Hardik Pandya has strengthened their all-round options and added depth to the batting order, the departure of Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians has left a significant void in their pace attack.Pujara believes the identity and quality of Arshdeep's replacement could prove decisive in determining Punjab's title prospects, with the franchise needing to build a bowling attack capable of delivering consistently throughout the tournament.Speaking to JioStar, Pujara highlighted the contrasting impact of Hardik's arrival and Arshdeep's departure, stressing that Punjab must prioritise their bowling requirements at the auction.Arshdeep Singh's replacement could hold the key For PBKS"The arrival of Hardik Pandya has been one huge positive for Punjab, though alongside it there is a slight negative as well, that Arshdeep Singh isn't there. Even though his performance last season wasn't as special as expected, given the way he is bowling right now, he is back in form."So that could be a big blow for Punjab, and who's going to be his replacement will be the deciding factor. Of course, with Hardik Pandya coming in, their batting strength will increase. How his bowling is coming along, we don't know yet, because he has been recovering from an injury."While his bowling will also be important, he can't be the lead bowler, he can be a supporting bowler. The bowlers they pick at the auction and how they shape up will determine whether they can go on to win the trophy," Pujara said.Hardik Pandya can solve PBKS' no. 6 and no. 7 concernsPujara also believes Hardik's presence could address one of Punjab's long-standing batting concerns, particularly their inability to find stability in the lower middle order when early wickets fall."With Hardik in the team, the slight issue they used to face of needing someone to stabilise the innings after early wickets fall is a role he can fulfil very well, solving Punjab's No. 6 and No. 7 problems," Pujara added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vedant Sehwag bags seven-wicket haul for brother Aaryavir-led Delhi in Cooch Behar Trophy
articles.summary: Vedant Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, made headlines with an impressive bowling performance for Delhi U-19 against Punjab U-19 in the
articles.body: Vedant Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, made headlines with an impressive bowling performance for Delhi U-19 against Punjab U-19 in the ongoing Cooch Behar Trophy Elite tournament.The youngster picked up seven wickets for 88 runs in 22.3 overs, including five maiden overs, to lead Delhi's bowling attack. His disciplined spell proved crucial as he ran through the Punjab batting line-up, making a significant impact in the ongoing four-day contest.Vedant Sehwag Leads Delhi's Bowling AttackVedant was the standout performer with the ball, claiming seven of the 10 wickets to fall. He maintained an impressive economy rate of 3.91 while bowling 22.3 overs.Nakul Yadav provided support with one wicket for 25 runs in seven overs, while Rahul Rakesh Yadav and Arnav Bugga also picked up a wicket each. Dweep Gahlot bowled 11 overs and conceded 32 runs without taking a wicket.Delhi U-19 trail Punjab by 134 runs at stumpsAt the end of the first day's play, Delhi U-19 were 104/2 in 40 overs in reply to Punjab's first-innings total of 238. The visitors were still trailing by 134 runs, with eight wickets remaining.Sahijbotveer Singh top-scored for Punjab with 61 off 116 deliveries, while Noorveer Singh contributed 58 off 58 balls. Sahijbotveer's innings included 10 boundaries, while Noorveer struck nine fours and two sixes. Meanwhile, captaimn Aaryavir Sehwag had a brief outing with 31 (94).Continuing Sehwag family's cricketing legacyVedant is following in the footsteps of his father, Virender Sehwag, who enjoyed a celebrated international career and established himself as one of India's most destructive opening batters. His elder brother, Aaryavir Sehwag, has also been making his mark in age-group cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Sooryavanshi will score 500 in a Test': Kevin Pietersen's jaw-dropping prediction for India's 15-year-old sensation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's extraordinary rise continues to attract attention from some of cricket's biggest names, with former England captain
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's extraordinary rise continues to attract attention from some of cricket's biggest names, with former England captain Kevin Pietersen making a staggering prediction about the 15-year-old batting sensation after his record-shattering double century in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026.Pietersen took to social media on Thursday to make a bold forecast about the teenager's future in the longest format, suggesting that Sooryavanshi could produce a monumental individual score in Test cricket in the coming years."Here’s a shout — Vaibhav will score a 500 in a Test Match within the next 5yrs!," Pietersen wrote on X.The prediction comes after Sooryavanshi delivered one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, smashing 204 off just 53 balls against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in India A's final group-stage match.Although the teenager could not replicate that astonishing performance in Thursday's semifinal against Sri Lanka A, his reputation continues to grow following a year in which he has rewritten several records.From 52-ball double century to Pietersen's 500-run predictionSooryavanshi's innings against the UAE was a record-breaking assault, featuring 28 sixes and seven fours. He reached his century in just 28 deliveries, brought up 150 in 40 balls and completed his double century in only 52 deliveries.The International Cricket Council confirmed that the 15-year-old had registered the fastest century and double century in men's List A cricket. His 200 came almost twice as quickly as the previous record of 103 balls.India A eventually chased down the UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, finishing at 254/3, with Sooryavanshi contributing more than 80 per cent of the team's total.After the innings, the teenager explained how he adjusted his approach after assessing the conditions.“In the last two matches, I got set but couldn’t convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren’t getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths,” he said.“There wasn’t anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn’t the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game,” he added.Sooryavanshi falls for 40 in semifinalThe teenager's remarkable run continued to be a talking point even though he managed only 40 off 27 balls against Sri Lanka A in the semifinal. His innings included four fours and three sixes, and he shared an explosive 80-run opening partnership with Abhishek Sharma in eight overs.Sooryavanshi was eventually dismissed in the eighth over, caught by Lasith Croospulle off Janith Liyanage while attempting to pull a short delivery.The latest exploits add to an extraordinary year for the youngster, who smashed 175 in India's Under-19 World Cup final triumph in February, made a significant impact in the IPL and became the youngest player to represent India in a full international match.With Pietersen now predicting a 500-run Test innings within five years, the spotlight on the teenage prodigy is only getting bigger.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
